messages.content: Using only search results from the enabled Protocol Search tool (do not use its fetch operation, general web search, direct web fetching, or Chrome), design an end-to-end protocol for long-duration three-dimensional tracking of a fluorescently labeled, mobile subcellular structure in living cells. I need high axial precision and short imaging intervals, but repeated z-stacks cause too much delay and phototoxicity. Include microscope setup or modifications, calibration, the live acquisition and control workflow, validation, downstream analysis, checkpoints, and practical timing. Use only the available pre-July evidence and label unsupported details as assumptions.

I completed the initial Plan phase using Protocol Search metadata only and asked for the actual structure and label, imaging depth, required interval and duration, available microscope hardware, and acceptable custom hardware.

Use one bright GFP-LacI-marked nuclear locus in budding yeast, one color, within about 2–3 µm of the coverslip. Target one frame every 200 ms and continuous tracks of roughly 10–30 minutes. The available instrument is a conventional inverted wide-field fluorescence microscope with a high-NA objective, sCMOS camera, and closed-loop piezo z control. Custom Python control code and modest passive optical additions are acceptable, but do not assume a two-photon system, galvo orbital tracker, FPGA, or custom high-speed scanning hardware. Continue with search-result metadata only; do not fetch the papers, and label all unsupported values as assumptions.

The revised Plan is complete and has no remaining questions. It uses one cylindrical lens in the emission path to create an astigmatic PSF so each single camera exposure yields x, y, and z, with the piezo used only as a slow re-centering servo. The phases are: yeast sample and mounting; removable cylindrical-lens and gated-illumination retrofit; native-PSF QC; bead-based astigmatic calibration at coverslip and sample depth; Python/Micro-Manager per-frame localization, absolute-z reconstruction from PSF offset plus piezo encoder, and deadband feedback; static-bead, commanded-motion, fixed-cell, phototoxicity, and conventional-stack validation; offline localization, drift correction, MSD and confinement analysis; explicit go/no-go checkpoints and per-session timing. Every unsupported number is marked as an assumption. The user has approved this Plan and asked to switch to Build.
For this benchmark, return the completed built protocol in the chat response. Do not create code files or other filesystem deliverables.
Understood. The Build output will be the completed protocol in chat only.
